I've been farming these 14 mu in Quzhou for 40 years now. I'm 65, my back isn't what it used to be, but I still know every inch of this land. My son works over in Handan at a factory, sends some money home, so we're not desperate for cash, but I still watch every yuan. My wife helps in the fields, and my daughter-in-law comes back during busy seasons. I finished middle school, so I can read the fertilizer labels and I listen to what the extension folks say, but honestly, after four decades, I trust my own eyes more than anyone's textbook.

This year I'm keeping 8 mu for wheat-maize like always. I'm planting the winter wheat in early October — same improved variety I used last year, the one from the seed shop that gave me about 480 kg per mu. For fertilizer, I'll put down about 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting — the 15-15-15 kind — and then topdress with about 15 kg of urea at jointing in spring. The extension guy says that gives about 15 kg of nitrogen per mu, which is about right for this soil. Last year I tried a bit more and didn't see much difference, so I'll stick with that. I'll irrigate three times: winter irrigation after the New Year if it's dry, then at jointing, then at heading. Each time the pump costs me about 20 yuan per mu, so I don't waste water.

For the summer maize, it goes in right after we harvest the wheat, usually around June 10th. Tight window — sometimes we only have three or four days. I hire the combine for wheat, costs about 60 yuan per mu, but it's worth it. Then I plant the maize with my small planter. Hybrid seed, about 3 kg per mu. One shot of compound fertilizer at planting, around 40 kg per mu. If the rains come good, maybe irrigate twice. Last year was dry, I had to pump twice.

Cotton is on 4 mu. I plant in late April with plastic mulch to keep the soil warm. Cotton is a pain for pests — the bollworm always comes. I spray insecticide four or five times, and use some herbicide too. Fertilizer is about the same as wheat, maybe a bit less nitrogen total, around 12 kg per mu. Cotton needs picking labor, which is the hard part. My family does most of it, but if my daughter-in-law can't come back during peak picking in September, I might have to hire a few days.

Garlic — I do 2 mu. It's good money when prices are right, but planting it kills your back — you have to push every clove into the ground by hand. I plant in early October, same time as wheat, so those two weeks are exhausting. I make raised beds for the garlic because it hates wet feet. Fertilizer is a bit heavier than grain — garlic is greedy, so I give it about 15 kg nitrogen per mu plus more phosphorus and potassium. I expect around 1,200 kg per mu if the weather holds, and I harvest in late June.

Total costs will run about 5,800 yuan for all inputs. That's manageable with my son's help, but I can't go much higher. I'd rather be a bit conservative than risk running out of cash for pumping if a drought hits.
